_note: Authored for this benchmark. WSI-FiVE publishes one question set and it is lung-specific: 'spread through air spaces' (STAS), 'pleural invasion' and 'excluding the current lung organ' have no kidney meaning. These six mirror the released set's role -- grading plus the local-extension findings that drive staging -- using concepts TCGA-RCC reports actually record (measured coverage in parentheses). A WSI-FiVE result on RCC is therefore not prompt-faithful.
questions: What is the nuclear grade of the tumour? (WHO/ISUP or Fuhrman grade 1-4, or Unknown.)
Is there any sarcomatoid or rhabdoid differentiation in the tumour?
Is there any indication of vascular or lymphovascular invasion, including renal vein involvement?
Is there any invasion of perinephric or renal sinus fat by the tumour?
Is the tumour confined within the renal capsule, or does it extend beyond it into adjacent structures?
Are the surgical margins of the resection clear of tumour? (note that: R0 means negative; R1 R2 both mean positive; Rx means Unknown.
